claims.text: Closed-loop machine-learning control using thermographic feedback can dynamically adjust laser power and scan path during laser powder bed fusion.
Dynamic adjustment of laser power and scan parameters will reduce thermal gradients in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Reduced thermal gradients will mitigate residual-stress accumulation.
The ML-controlled regime will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Real-time adaptive control will simplify processing relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed feedstock is gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy or multi-principal-element alloy powder with a particle-size range of 10–53 µm.
An applicable processing window is approximately 50–100 W laser power, 200–800 mm/s scanning speed, and 20 µm layer thickness.
The stated processing window will maintain stable, low-temperature melt pools.
The intervention applies to miniature parts up to approximately 10 mm in characteristic dimension.
ML-guided process adjustment will reduce local defects in the as-built material.
Continuous monitoring and laser-parameter adjustment will moderate peak temperatures.
Continuous monitoring and laser-parameter adjustment will moderate solidification rates.
Moderating peak temperatures and solidification rates will decrease thermal shock and residual-stress formation.
Reduced thermal shock and residual stress will improve structural coherence and mechanical performance without complex secondary processing.
Conventional fixed-parameter, high-power laser powder bed fusion produces large thermal gradients and high residual stresses.
Relative to the conventional baseline, ML-controlled components will have measurably lower residual stress.
Relative to the conventional baseline, ML-controlled components will exhibit increased yield strength and ductility.
The intervention will be most effective for geometries below 10 mm because such geometries have previously experienced unacceptably high stress buildup from elevated thermal gradients.
Improvements may be smaller for larger builds or different powder compositions.
